# Carlos Trujillo — Marketing Scientist

> Carlos Trujillo is a marketing scientist specialising in Bayesian causal inference, marketing mix modeling (MMM) and budget optimization. He works at Wise (Tallinn) and PyMC Labs (remote). This file lists the site's key content as clean Markdown mirrors (URL + `.md`) for LLM consumption at inference time.

Notes:

- Topics covered: Bayesian statistics, causal inference, quasi-experiments, marketing mix modeling, prior elicitation, budget/risk optimization, symbolic computing and local LLM inference. Implemented in Python with PyMC, PyMC-Marketing and PyTensor.
- Each link below has a clean Markdown version at the same URL with `.md` appended (e.g. `about.html.md`).

## Pages

- [Home](https://cetagostini.github.io/index.html.md): Overview, recent articles and upcoming talks.
- [About](https://cetagostini.github.io/about.html.md): Bio, career history (as a DAG), education and skills.
- [Articles index](https://cetagostini.github.io/articles.html.md): All articles with dates and topic tags.
- [Diary](https://cetagostini.github.io/diary.html.md): Daily progress notes and random stuff (Bayesian methods, causal inference, side quests). Newest first.
- [Talks](https://cetagostini.github.io/talks.html.md): Recorded conference talks and webinars.

## Articles

- [Media Does Not Stop at the City Border: Cross-City Spillovers with PyMC-Marketing](https://cetagostini.github.io/articles/custom-article/custom-article.html.md): Sparse, bounded cross-city media spillovers in a multidimensional PyMC-Marketing MMM using a custom MuEffect and MaskedPrior. August 2026.
- [PyTensor Beyond PyMC: Building LLM Inference in Python](https://cetagostini.github.io/articles/alchemize_pytensor_mlx_gemma_3n/alchemize_pytensor_mlx_gemma_3n.html.md): Building and validating Gemma 3n inference from one symbolic PyTensor graph compiled through C/CVM, Numba and MLX. July 2026.
- [Can You Trust Your Quasi-Experiment? A Bayesian Framework for Auditing Time-Series Causal Estimates](https://cetagostini.github.io/articles/placebo_bayesian_quasi_experiments/placebo_bayesian_quasi_experiments.html.md): Bayesian placebo tests with ROPE-based inference to audit quasi-experimental causal estimates. April 2026.
- [Decision-Making Under Contradictions: Robust Budget Allocation When Your Models Disagree](https://cetagostini.github.io/articles/decision_making_under_contradictions/decision_making_under_contradictions.html.md): Robust budget allocation when MMM, experiments and attribution disagree. February 2026.
- [From Experiments to Priors: Eliciting Informative Priors for Your Marketing Mix Model](https://cetagostini.github.io/articles/from_experiments_to_priors/from_experiments_to_priors.html.md): Translating quasi-experimental results into informative Bayesian priors for an MMM using CausalPy and PyMC-Marketing. February 2026.
- [Bayesian Models and Risk Optimization](https://cetagostini.github.io/articles/bayesian_models_and_risk_optimization/bayesian_models_and_risk_optimization.html.md): Risk-aware budget optimization with Bayesian models. PyData Berlin 2025. August 2025.
- [No More Experiments Without Causality](https://cetagostini.github.io/articles/nomore_experiments_without_causality/nomore_experiments_without_causality.html.md): Why media mix model calibration is useless without causal knowledge. PyData DE Darmstadt 2025. April 2025.
- [Baby Steps for Causal Discovery](https://cetagostini.github.io/articles/baby_steps_for_causal_discovery/baby_steps_for_causal_discovery.html.md): An introduction to causal discovery for marketing and data science. PyData Tallinn 2025. February 2025.
